learning_objective: 🎯 Dive deep into the magnetic properties of different materials, uncover the secrets of Earth's magnetic field, and understand the behavior of bar magnets!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A bar magnet acts like a magnetic dipole with a North and South pole. Unlike electric charges, magnetic monopoles do not exist—if you cut a magnet in half, you just get two smaller magnets, each with its own N and S pole!

Earth acts like a giant magnet. To fully describe Earth's magnetic field at any place, we need three elements: Magnetic Declination, Magnetic Dip (or Inclination), and the Horizontal Component of Earth's field.

Materials react to magnetic fields differently. Diamagnetic materials weakly repel magnets. Paramagnetic materials are weakly attracted. Ferromagnetic materials (like iron) are strongly attracted and can become permanent magnets.
When a material is placed in a magnetic field, it gets magnetized. Magnetic Susceptibility tells us how easily a substance responds to an external magnetic field.

For ferromagnetic materials, the magnetization lags behind the applied magnetic field. When the external field is removed, it retains some magnetism (Retentivity). The reverse field needed to completely demagnetize it is called Coercivity.

fun_activity.title: 🗺️ Iron Filings Art
fun_activity.instructions: Place a bar magnet under a piece of white paper. Lightly sprinkle iron filings on top of the paper and tap it gently. The filings will perfectly align to reveal the invisible, beautiful curved magnetic field lines!

exam_tips: 📌 A very common question is to compare Dia, Para, and Ferromagnetic substances. Make a 3-column table memorizing their susceptibility and permeability values.
📌 For permanent magnets, choose materials with High Retentivity and High Coercivity (like steel). For electromagnets, choose Low Retentivity and Low Coercivity (like soft iron).
📌 Remember Gauss's law for magnetism: The net magnetic flux through any closed surface is always zero (because magnetic monopoles don't exist).
quick_recap: ⭐ Magnetic poles always exist in pairs. There is no such thing as an isolated North pole.
⭐ Earth's magnetic North pole is actually physically near the geographic South pole!
⭐ Ferromagnetic materials lose their strong magnetic properties when heated above their 'Curie Temperature'.
